name: io.github.christopherjjellison-maker/zorvu
title: Zorvu
description: Pre-sign checks and Stock Token sell depth for Robinhood Chain: drainer code, lookalikes, fills

tools.name: precheck_transaction
tools.description:
Check a Robinhood Chain transaction before it is signed. Send the transaction you are about to sign and get back `pass`, `warn` or `block` with the reasons behind it.

It covers transactions that approve, transfer or swap a token on Robinhood Chain (chain 4663), including approvals to a new spender. It flags drainer contracts, broad approvals to unknown spenders, lookalike Stock Tokens (read live from the token's own ticker and name), and a size larger than the pools can take. Zorvu does not grade the liquidity, holders or sellability of tokens that are not official Stock Tokens: such a token comes back `token_not_graded` (info), and archived readings never count as a pass. `intent.usd` checks the size against measured sell depth, and `policy` applies the caller's own ceilings.

`pass` means the transaction passed the checks listed in `checks_run` at the time shown in `checked_at`, nothing broader. It does not mean the transaction is safe, and it is not a promise about what the transaction will do. `warn` and `block` are Zorvu's measurements, not instructions and not advice; the decision stays with the caller. Every reason carries a `finding_type`; `verdict` classifies those findings, and `decision_owner` is always `caller`. Zorvu never builds, routes, signs or sends a transaction, holds no keys, and charges no fee.

Anything Zorvu could not read comes back `null` with a reason code saying so, never as a pass. `mode: "fast"` skips live chain reads; what it gives up is listed in each `not_checked_fast` reason. Requires a Zorvu API key, sent in the Authorization header of the MCP client config; the tool takes no key argument. Not financial advice.

chain_id.description: Robinhood Chain. The only chain supported.

mode.description: fast: no live chain reads, for an answer in well under a second.

tx.description: The transaction you are about to sign.

usd.description: Intended size in USD, checked against measured sell depth.

receipt.description: true keeps a receipt of this answer and returns its id and url, readable later with get_receipt. Off by default; nothing is kept without it.

tools.name: stock_sell_depth
tools.description:
Zorvu's estimate of how much of an official Robinhood Chain Stock Token could be sold on-chain right now, and at what price against the reference price. Returns the estimated fills at $1,000, $10,000 and $100,000, and the largest size the pools took within 2% and within 5% of the reference price. Give a ticker or an address; a ticker resolves only to the official token, never to a lookalike.

Useful before sizing a sell, a liquidation or an on-chain unwind, and for valuing a Stock Token as collateral or margin. `impact_pct` is the fill against the reference price: negative is below it (`-0.82` means a $10,000 sell was estimated to fill 0.82% below), positive is above it, when the pools trade at a premium to the reference.

Every figure carries the time it was measured and its age in seconds. Readings older than 30 minutes, and max-size searches older than 2 hours, are reported as no reading rather than as a number: a missing figure is unknown, never to be read as zero or as deep. `capped: true` means the search stopped at its ceiling, so the real size is at least that large. These are estimates: each figure is a measurement of a sell quote, not of a fill — not a quote you can take, not a promise of what you could sell now, and not advice. Zorvu does not total liquidity across tokens: a pool pairing two Stock Tokens counts toward both.

symbol.description: Ticker, for example NVDA. Resolves only to the official Stock Token, never to a lookalike.

address.description: Contract address of an official Stock Token.

inputSchema.description: Give exactly one of symbol or address.

tools.name: check_token
tools.description:
Zorvu's automated risk check on any Robinhood Chain token: the grade, each check that ran with its result and reason, a drainer-code check, and when every underlying reading was taken.

It covers any token address. For a whole transaction, `precheck_transaction` also decodes the calldata and checks the spender.

The drainer-code check reads the contract's own code from the chain, once per contract and then reused (a contract's code does not change after it is deployed): `drainer_check` carries `cached` and `read_at` when the answer is a reading Zorvu took earlier, so the time of the read is always in the answer. The official Stock Token lookalike check (on the token's live `symbol()` and `name()`) runs live. Zorvu's other token measurements (liquidity, holders, sell test, deployer history) are archived readings: an archived reading never counts as a pass, may support a warn or a fail for 7 days with its date in `reading_at`, and is not used after that. `token_data` says which applies (`archived` or `none`). The grade says what those checks measured at the time shown; it never means the token is safe or safe to buy, and it is not a recommendation. While Zorvu's token measurements are an archive the grade is `Not yet checked`, `Limited data`, `Elevated risk`, `High risk`, or `Not applicable` for a base asset of the chain. It is never `Low risk` today, so `passed_zorvu_safety_checks` is `false` on every answer: it carries no signal and does not mean the token failed. A check Zorvu could not run is `no_data` or `inconclusive`, never a pass. These are measurements, not advice; they may be incomplete, wrong or out of date. Not financial advice.

address.description: Token contract address on Robinhood Chain.

tools.name: find_stock_token
tools.description:
Resolve a stock ticker (for example `NVDA`) to the official Robinhood Chain Stock Token contract address, with a count of the known lookalike contracts using that ticker.

A ticker is not an address, and impostor contracts reuse real tickers: the `address` this returns is the official contract, and a lookalike is a different contract with the same name.

`lookalikes` is how many impostor contracts Zorvu's scan has seen for this ticker, with the time of that scan in `lookalikes_at`. A lookalike's `liq_peak` is the highest liquidity ever seen for it, not what it holds now. An unknown ticker comes back as not an official Stock Token rather than guessed at. These are registry and scan measurements, not advice. Zorvu is not affiliated with Robinhood Markets, Inc. or its affiliates.

tools.name: get_receipt
tools.description:
Read back a Zorvu Shield receipt by its id: the record of a pre-sign check that was kept at the caller's request, with the verdict, the reason codes with what kind of finding each was (`finding_type`, null on a receipt kept before Zorvu recorded it), the checks that ran, what each checked token came back as, and the time of every reading the verdict rested on.

Useful for showing what was checked before a transaction was signed, or for verifying a receipt someone hands over. A receipt exists only when the precheck call asked for one with `receipt: true`; nothing is kept otherwise and there is no way to list receipts. The id is the only access control, so it works like a link to a private page.

`response_sha256` makes the record tamper-evident: drop `response_sha256` and `disclaimer`, sort the remaining keys, serialise with no whitespace, SHA-256 that, and it matches. `request_sha256` is the hash of the request body as Zorvu received it, so whoever holds that body can prove which transaction was checked. Zorvu does not keep the body itself, the sender, the calldata, the intended size or the caller's own policy. The `to` address is kept only when Zorvu's code read found contract code at it: `to_kind` says `contract`, `wallet` or `unknown`, and for the last two the address itself is not in the receipt at all.

A receipt is a measurement of what Zorvu's checks returned at that time. It is not an audit, a certification or a guarantee, and not financial advice.

id.description: The receipt id a precheck_transaction call returned in receipt.id.

tools.name: scan_wallet
tools.description:
Read what a wallet holds on Robinhood Chain and say, token by token, which contracts use the ticker of an official Stock Token without being it, which hold code Zorvu's check reads as a drainer, which are the official Stock Tokens, and how large a sale the pools took for those.

Useful for telling a holding apart from an impostor of it before anything is signed, and for seeing at once which of a wallet's positions Zorvu has any reading for. `summary.line` is the one-sentence count; `tokens` is every holding, with the lookalikes first.

The wallet is read live and is not stored: Zorvu keeps no record of the address or of the result. The scan reads balances once from the chain and everything else from its own stored readings, so it makes no per-token chain read: a token Zorvu has no reading for comes back with `group: "unknown"`, `drainer_check: null` and no ticker. A null is no reading — never a pass, never zero, and never that the code is clean. Each reading carries the time it was taken and where it came from. Whether a token can be sold at all is not checked here. Balances are raw on-chain integers with no decimals applied, and when the list comes from Transfer logs there is no balance at all and a token the wallet has since sent on can still appear. At most 100 tokens, with `balances.truncated` saying when a wallet held more. These are measurements of public chain data at the time shown, not advice and not a recommendation about any holding.

wallet.description: The wallet address to read, on Robinhood Chain. It is read live and is not stored.

tools.name: simulate_sell
tools.description:
Simulate selling a Robinhood Chain token and see whether it can be sold at all. Zorvu gives a throwaway address the tokens in a counterfactual read of the chain and tries the sell through the token's deepest pool. Nothing is signed, nothing is sent, no transaction is built and no keys are involved.

Use it before accepting a token as collateral, before sizing an exit, or to catch a token that can be bought but not sold. It covers any token address, not only official Stock Tokens.

`sellable` is `true`, `false` or `"unknown"`, and the three mean different things. `false` is a finding: the sell was refused by the token's own code on a rig that was proven to work on that same token moments earlier. `"unknown"` means Zorvu could not establish either answer, and `reason` says why -- it is never to be read as a pass or as a failure. `true` means one simulated sell of that size returned tokens at the time shown; it does not mean the token is safe, and it is not a promise about a real sale, which happens at a different block against a different pool state.

`impact_pct` compares the fill with a dust-sized sell through the same route: `-4.2` means the simulated size filled 4.2% worse than dust did. `reference_price` and the amounts are ratios of raw token units, and `implied_sell_tax_bps` is not measured in this version -- a tax cannot be told apart from the pool's own fee without the pool's mid price, so it is reported as unknown rather than estimated. Every answer carries `read_at`. Requires a Zorvu API key in the Authorization header of your MCP client config; the tool takes no key argument. Not financial advice.

address.description: Contract address of the token to try selling. Any Robinhood Chain token, not only an official Stock Token.

usd.description: Size to simulate selling, in US dollars. Applied only when the deepest pool is quoted in a dollar stablecoin; otherwise a fraction of the pool is used and size_usd_applied is false.

inputSchema.description: Give the token address. usd defaults to 1000.
